---
title: "multised (slim)"
subtitle: "Harmonised marine-sediment trace-element data from five sources"
---

**multised** assembles a database of marine-sediment trace-element measurements
from five external sources, harmonises them into a common schema, and
progressively quality-controls the result. This site documents the **slim**
stage: five per-source databases that share one common schema, together with the
quality-control and marking work performed on them.

## Data sources

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(knitr)

sources_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Source,      ~Origin,            ~Notes,
  "Mareano",    "Norway / IMR",     "Norwegian cruise data.",
  "Vannmiljø",  "Norway",           "Norwegian environmental monitoring.",
  "ICES-DOME",  "International",     "Rich sediment-composition data.",
  "MUDAB",      "Germany",           "German marine environmental database.",
  "4Demon",     "Belgium",           "Compiled historical Baltic/North Sea data (Belgian)."
)

kable(sources_tbl)
```

Each source was first parsed into a per-source **pilot** database (documented on
its own pilot site), then reshaped into the shared **slim** schema used here.

## Pipeline generations

The data moves through four generations, each one SQLite database **per source**
until the final merge:

1. **pilot**: each source's raw files parsed into a per-source database whose
   table structure follows that source. Documented on the individual pilot sites:
   [Mareano](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mareano-pilot/),
   [Vannmiljø](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/vannmiljo-pilot/),
   [ICES-DOME](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/ices-dome-pilot/),
   [MUDAB](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mudab-pilot/), and
   [4Demon](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/4demon-pilot/).
2. **slim** *(this site)*: every source reshaped into the same seven-table
   schema, then annotated with quality-control and marking flags. The underlying
   values are untouched; suspicious records are *flagged*, not deleted, so they
   can be reviewed.
3. **clean**: the flags are applied (uncertain rows removed), units are
   harmonised, and normalisation (Fe/Al) and grain-size analyses are run.
4. **merged**: the five clean databases are combined into a single database for
   the background / pristine-sediment analysis.

## What this site covers

The slim schema, the quality-control flagging, and the construction of the clean
databases are all documented here, grouped in the navigation bar:

**DB Design**

- [DB Schema (Slim)](./db-schema-slim.qmd): the common seven-table schema, the
  entity-relationship diagram, and a per-source column comparison showing which
  columns are shared and which are source-specific.
- [DB Schema (Clean)](./db-schema-clean.qmd): the clean database table layout.
- [Database Downloads](./database-downloads.qmd): download links for the five
  slim SQLite databases.

**Flagging** (the quality-control and marking work)

- [Class Summary](./class-summary.qmd): the measurand categories (target,
  reference, organic, composition) that later steps read.
- [Unit Conversion & Range Check](./flagging-conversion-range.qmd): the
  standardised value/unit and the per-element plausible-range flag.
- [Common Flags](./flagging-common.qmd): the flags shared by every source
  (invalid values, duplicates, below-LOQ, multi-layer, weight basis, and more).
- [Source Specific](./flagging-source-specific.qmd): each source's native
  leftover flags that the common flags do not cover.

**Grain Size**

- [Sample Fraction (matrix)](./grain-size-fraction.qmd): whether each sample is a
  whole (bulk) sediment or a sieved fraction.
- [Fines (<63 µm)](./grain-size-fines.qmd): deriving the clay + silt fines
  fraction, including the noisy-curve correction.

**Clean Databases** (how the QC-passed end product is built)

- [Overview](./clean-overview.qmd): the three-step clean stage and what the
  cleaning removed.
- [Harmonisation](./clean-harmonisation.qmd), [Cleaning](./clean-cleaning.qmd),
  and [Grain-size Tables](./clean-grain-size.qmd): the individual steps.
- [Cleaning Summary](./clean-cleaning-summary.qmd): chemistry counts before and
  after cleaning, overall and per element.
